questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word similar in meaning to the word given. **

Monotonous
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option1, i.e. Dull.

The given word i.e. ‘Monotonous’ means ‘dull, tedious, and repetitious; lacking in variety and interest’ and is synonymous with the word ‘dull’. ‘Timid’ means ‘showing lack of courage’ and ‘unfriendly’ means something or someone that is not friendly and ‘lusty’ means ‘healthy and strong’. Since, all the options except 1 are out of context with the given word ‘monotonous’ thus, can be eliminated.

questions.question:
**Improve the bracketed part of the sentence. **

(Being a pleasant evening), we went out for a long drive on a highway.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2, i.e. It being a pleasant evening.

The original sentence is grammatically correct, but it can be improved by adding a subject to the sentence.

Option 2 provides a subject "it" to the sentence which makes it more clear and concise.

The phrase "**it being**" acts as a subject in the sentence and makes the sentence more grammatically sound.

Option 1 is also grammatically correct, but it sounds a little awkward. Option 3 changes the meaning of the sentence and doesn't fit well in the context

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'. **

The Tata group owns (1)/ many industries, that are spread (2)/ across the globe. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2, i.e. 2.

In the given sentence the comma (,) after industries is misplaced and should be removed. Also, ‘industries’ must be replaced with ‘companies’ as the word industry is usually used for many companies that are into the same kind/area of business. For example, the steel industry, auto industry etc..

Hence, the statement can be correctly rewritten as, The Tata group owns many companies that are spread across the globe.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word opposite in meaning to the word given. **

Colossal
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Colossal"** means something extremely large or great. (विशालकाय)

 
 
• **Example: **The ancient pyramids are colossal structures that attract millions of tourists every year.
 
 
 
• **"Teeny"** refers to something very small or tiny. (बहुत छोटा)
 
 
• **Example: **The newborn kitten was so teeny that it could fit in the palm of my hand.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the opposite of **'Colossal' **is **'Teeny'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Epic** (महाकाव्य): A long narrative poem, often written about a hero or heroic events.

 
 
• **Example:** Homer's Iliad is an epic that has been studied for centuries.
 
 
 
• **Rust** (जंग): A reddish-brown coating formed on iron or steel by oxidation, especially in the presence of moisture.
 
 
• **Example:** The old bicycle was covered in rust after being left out in the rain for years.
 
 
 
• **Vast** (विशाल): Of very great extent or quantity; immense.
 
 
• **Example:** The Sahara Desert is a vast expanse of sand and dunes.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word opposite in meaning to the word given. **

Opprobrium
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** option 1, i.e. Adulation.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"opprobrium" **means **harsh criticism or public disgrace, **and the opposite of it is** "adulation," **which means** excessive praise or admiration.**
 
• **Examples:**
 
 
• The actor's performance was met with great **adulation **from the audience.
 
• The politician's decision to accept the bribe was met with public **opprobrium**.
 
 
 
• **Option 2, "ignominy,"** is a synonym of "**opprobrium**" and means **disgrace or dishonor.** It is not the opposite of "opprobrium."
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 3, "mystical,"** is unrelated to the meaning of "opprobrium" and means having a spiritual or mystical nature.
 
• **Option 4, "preclude,"** means to prevent or make impossible, and is not the opposite of "opprobrium."
 
• **Examples:**
 
 
• The athlete suffered **ignominy **when she was caught using performance-enhancing drugs.
 
• The **mystical **atmosphere of the ancient temple filled the tourists with a sense of awe.
 
• The lack of funding will **preclude **the construction of the new library.
 
 
 
• Note that options 2, 3, and 4 are all unrelated to the meaning of "opprobrium."

questions.question: If so, English is perhaps the most _____ lens through which to see animals.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**distorting**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In this context, '**distorting**' is the most fitting word to complete the sentence "If so, English is perhaps the most _____ lens through which to see animals."
 
• The word 'distorting' refers to the act of twisting or altering something out of its true, natural, or original state.
 
• The context implies that the English language may create a skewed or misrepresented view of animals.
 
• Hence, the correct answer will be **Option 1.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• '**Distorting**' means giving a misleading or false account or impression of something. It fits the context best, as it suggests that the English language may change or warp the way animals are seen.

 
 
• Example sentence: The mirror was distorting his reflection.
 
 
 
• '**Disturbing**' means causing distress or worry or upsetting. This doesn't fit into the context of the lens or perspective through which we see animals.
 
 
• Example sentence: It was a disturbing news report.
 
 
 
• '**Popular**' means liked or admired by many people or by a particular person or group. This doesn't fit into the context of the sentence which implies a characteristic of the lens, not its popularity.
 
 
• Example sentence: She's a popular singer among teenagers.
 
 
 
• '**Useful**' means able to be used for a practical purpose or in several ways. In this context, it doesn't fit as it doesn't imply any form of alteration or misrepresentation in the way animals are seen.
 
 
• Example sentence: This guidebook is very useful for new travelers.

questions.question: The very word "animal" can _____ the brutish and the sensual.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1, i.e. connote.

‘Connote’ means ‘(of a word) imply or suggest (an idea or feeling) in addition to the literal or primary meaning’. It logically fits the blank well and coveys the meaning of the sentence in the sense as the very word ‘animal’ can imply or suggest (connote) the brutish and the sensual. Other options are irrelevant and can be rejected.

Hence, the statement can be rewritten as, The very word "animal" can connote the brutish and the sensual.

questions.question: Animal _____ imply baseness and vulgarity.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'instincts'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given context, '**instincts**' would be the most fitting word to complete the sentence "Animal _____ imply baseness and vulgarity."
 
• The word 'instincts' is used to refer to inherent inclinations of a living organism towards a particular complex behavior.
 
• In reference to animals, it could mean behaviors driven by primal urges or natural tendencies.
 
• Hence, the correct answer will be **Option 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• '**Breeding**' refers to the reproduction and raising of animals, or more generally the cultivation of plants and animals. This doesn't fit into the context of implying baseness and vulgarity.

 
 
• **Example sentence:** The farmer has been breeding cattle for many years.
 
 
 
• '**Gestures**' means the use of motions of the limbs or body as a means of expression, usually related to humans and not commonly used for animals.
 
 
• **Example sentence: **The politician's gestures were animated as he delivered his speech.
 
 
 
• '**Instincts**' refers to an innate, typically fixed pattern of behavior in animals in response to certain stimuli. In the context of the sentence, this could imply baseness and vulgarity because it refers to the inherent, often unrefined behaviors of animals.
 
 
• **Example sentence: **Cats have an instinct to hunt.
 
 
 
• '**Species**' refers to a group of living organisms consisting of similar individuals capable of exchanging genes or interbreeding. This does not fit into the context of implying baseness and vulgarity.
 
 
• **Example sentence**: The panda bear is an endangered species.

questions.question:
**In the following question, a sentence has been given in Active/Passive voice. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active voice. **

Rohan was not told about the e-mail.

options.text: Nobody told Rohan about the e-mail.
Somebody did not tell Rohan about the e-mail
The e-mail was not told about to Rohan.
There was nobody who could tell Rohan about the e-mail.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1, i.e. Nobody told Rohan about the e-mail.

Option 2 can be rejected as it introduces ‘someone’ who has no role to play in the given sentence. Moreover, it gives the impression that someone didn’t tell him about the mail deliberately. Further, options 3 and 4 can also be rejected as 3 seems to be grammatically inappropriate and does not follow the flow of ideas whereas, 4 also unnecessarily introduces ‘nobody who could’ as we are not dealing with the tendency, to tell the truth. Option 1 captures the flow of the idea in the most appropriate manner and is both grammatically and contextually correct.

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'. **

She has not been (1)/ to the restaurant (2)/ much late. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3, i.e. 3.

‘Much late’ is grammatically incorrect and must be replaced with ‘of late’ which signifies the event or the actions which happened a short time ago or recently. For example, His life has changed of late.

Hence, the statement can be correctly rewritten as She has not been to the restaurant of late.
